newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa says 22 could have died in diamond mine.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa says 22 could have died in diamond mine.

text.p: The death toll in a South African mining disaster could reach 22, a government minister said on Friday.

South African Mineral and Energy Affairs Minister Penuell Maduna said four bodies had been recovered and 18 miners were still unaccounted for after a mudslide late on Wednesday at a diamond mine in Free State province.
The underground mudslide followed heavy rains at the Roberts Victor Diamond Mine, owned by Vancouver-listed Botswana Diamondfields Inc.
Thirty-four miners were rescued, Maduna said in a statement.
"I sincerely hope that those still unaccounted for will be spared," the minister said, adding he would visit the mine with the government mining engineer Dick Bakker on Friday.
Mine officials have said there is no hope of finding the missing miners alive.

Rescue teams abandoned their search for other survivors on Thursday after it became too dangerous to continue, as mud was still flowing into the mine. Mining officials said there was little hope that other miners would have survived the mud crash.
An inquiry will be held to probe the cause of the disaster near Dealesville, some 60 km (38 miles) west of the provincial capital Bloemfontein.
